> Fit one random-intercept mixed model per feature on a latent scale (such as the log-odds of a site's occupancy), where each sample is either measured on that scale or counted through it (k of n trials succeed), and test each named coefficient with a Wald t.

Wire verb `stats fit-latent-mixed` · Python [`pymzlib.stats.fit_latent_mixed`][pymzlib.stats.fit_latent_mixed]

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `responses` | `path` | absent | latent units (e.g. natural log-odds of occupancy) | — | The measured samples: stats fit-mixed's responses table, a TSV with a header row, the feature id first (unique) and then one column per sample, named by its header. Values are on the LATENT scale (logit occupancy, for example), not fractions or intensities. A blank cell, NA or NaN (any case) is not measured. At least one of responses and counts is required. Absent, no sample is measured: the bridge passes an all-missing matrix of the counts' shape. |
| `counts` | `path` | absent | trials (successes of trials) | `each cell k/n, two whole numbers` | The counted samples (mzLib's BinomialCount): a TSV laid out as responses, each cell successes/trials such as 3/8, or blank, NA or NaN for a sample not counted. When both tables are given they must list exactly the same feature ids and sample columns, in any order (the responses' order is kept), and a cell may be measured or counted, not both (mzLib's rule). mzLib refuses a count with no trials, or more successes than trials. Absent, no sample is counted, and the model is stats fit-mixed's. |
| `design` | `path` | required | — | — | stats fit's design table: one row per sample, the sample name (matching the fit's sample columns exactly, rows matched by name) then one column per fixed-effect coefficient, every cell a finite number. Include an intercept column if you want one; do not add a column per group, which the random intercept replaces. mzLib refuses a design that is not of full column rank over all samples. |
| `groups` | `path` | required | — | — | stats fit-mixed's groups table: one row per sample, the sample name then EXACTLY ONE column, the sample's group label (an animal, a donor, a dataset), whose header names the grouping. The sample names must be exactly the fit's sample columns. Labels are trimmed and compared exactly; mzLib refuses an empty one. |
| `link` | `string` | required | natural log-odds | `identity, or 2 to 4 comma-separated numbers: intercept,slope[,depth_slope[,overdispersion]]` | mzLib's DetectionLink: how the latent value sets the chance g that one trial of a counted cell succeeds, logit g = intercept + slope x latent + depth_slope x depth, with trials in a cell correlated by overdispersion (rho, a beta-binomial; 0 is the binomial). REQUIRED: mzLib's link parameter has no default. identity is DetectionLink.Identity, (0, 1): a counted cell then samples the same probability a measured one reads. Numbers are passed as the record's positional arguments, so a depth_slope or overdispersion left out is the record's own default (0 at cc67b7a2). stats fit-link fits one from cells. mzLib refuses a non-finite intercept or depth slope, a slope that is 0 or not finite, and an overdispersion outside [0, 1). |
| `depth` | `path` | absent | depth units (the caller's, e.g. log2 target PSMs) | — | A TSV with a header row and one row per sample: the sample name (exactly the fit's samples, in any order), then one number, the sample's depth for the link's depth term. Needed when the link's depth_slope is not 0 (mzLib refuses otherwise). Absent, the bridge passes none. |
| `residual_variance` (wire `--residual-variance`) | `path` | absent | squared latent units | `each > 0 and finite, or blank to estimate` | A TSV with a header row and one row per feature: the feature id, then sigma^2 to use for it instead of estimating it (e.g. borrowed when a feature has too few measured samples). A blank, NA or NaN cell, or a feature not listed, is NaN, which mzLib reads as estimate it. An id that is not one of the fit's features is refused. Absent, the bridge passes none and every sigma^2 is estimated. |
| `stdin` | `string[]` | required | — | `>= 1 line; each a design column name, none repeated` | The coefficients to report, one design column name per line. The model always fits every design column; the table holds one block of rows per coefficient named here, in this order. |
| `estimator` | `string` | absent | — | `reml \| ml` | reml is VarianceEstimator.Reml (the fixed effects integrated out by a Laplace approximation, as glmmTMB's REML; exact when nothing is counted), ml is VarianceEstimator.MaximumLikelihood. Absent, the bridge sends none and LogitNormalMixedModel.Fit's default applies (Reml at cc67b7a2); the envelope's estimator says which was used. |
| `threads` | `int` | `1` | threads | `>= 1, or -1 for every core` | Features fitted at once. The bridge default is 1 (BULK.md); mzLib's own default is -1. Results are identical at any value (mzLib). |

### Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `responses_file` | `string` | — | yes: no --responses: nothing was measured | Absolute path of the responses table. |
| `counts_file` | `string` | — | yes: no --counts: nothing was counted | Absolute path of the counts table. |
| `design_file` | `string` | — | never | Absolute path of the design table. |
| `groups_file` | `string` | — | never | Absolute path of the groups table. |
| `depth_file` | `string` | — | yes: no --depth was given | Absolute path of the depth table. |
| `residual_variance_file` | `string` | — | yes: no --residual-variance: every sigma^2 was estimated | Absolute path of the residual-variance table. |
| `grouping` | `string` | — | never | The groups file's label column header. |
| `group_names` | `string[]` | — | never | The distinct labels, in order of first appearance over the samples (the order mzLib numbers them in). |
| `group_count` | `int` | groups | never | Distinct labels over all samples. A feature's own count is its groups column. |
| `feature_count` | `int` | features | never | Feature rows read. |
| `sample_count` | `int` | samples | never | Sample columns read. |
| `sample_names` | `string[]` | — | never | In the responses header's order (the counts header's, with counts alone): the order the design, group and depth rows were put in. |
| `coefficient_names` | `string[]` | — | never | Every design column, in order. |
| `tested_coefficients` | `string[]` | — | never | The stdin coefficients, in order; the table holds one block of feature_count rows per entry. |
| `estimator` | `string` | — | never | reml or ml: the estimator mzLib reports it fitted with (LogitNormalMixedModelFit.Estimator), the default when --estimator was absent. |
| `link` | `object` | — | never | The link every count cell was read through, as mzLib reports it (LogitNormalMixedModelFit.Link); fields under result.tables.link. |
| `threads` | `int` | threads | never | The thread count used. |
| `measured_cells` | `int` | cells | never | Feature x sample cells with a finite response. |
| `counted_cells` | `int` | cells | never | Feature x sample cells with a count. |
| `missing_count` | `int` | cells | never | Cells with neither a response nor a count, left out of their feature's fit. |
| `status_counts` | `map<string,int>` | features | never | Features per status, always these six keys: fitted, too_few_observations, rank_deficient, separated, not_converged, too_few_groups. They are the outcomes LogitNormalMixedModel.Fit's body can return at cc67b7a2; a stop-gap until mzLib says per model (mzLib#1487). |
| `row_count` | `int` | rows | never | feature_count x the number of tested coefficients. |
| `column_names` | `string[]` | — | never | The table's columns, in order. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | never | One row per (tested coefficient, feature): coefficient blocks in stdin order, features in file order. |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | Seven static caveats (one names the link used, one the estimator), plus one each, with counts, when any feature was not fitted, when a fitted row has no df, when a fitted feature's group_variance is 0, when any residual variance was given, and when nothing was counted. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `feature` | `string` | — | never | The feature id from the first column. |
| `coefficient` | `string` | — | never | The coefficient this row reports. |
| `status` | `string` | — | never | fitted \| too_few_observations (no more samples with a response of either kind than coefficients) \| rank_deficient (the design over those samples is not of full rank) \| separated (no estimate exists: a coefficient beyond +-SeparationLimit, 30 at cc67b7a2, on the latent scale, a Hessian that is not positive definite, or nothing measured and every group's counts one-sided, all 0 or all full) \| not_converged (the variance search failed, or the likelihood could not be evaluated at its optimum) \| too_few_groups (fewer than two groups, or none with two samples). Only fitted rows carry statistics. |
| `estimate` | `float` | latent units per coefficient unit (natural log-odds for a logit latent) | yes: status is not fitted | The fixed-effect coefficient at the estimated variances: the effect within groups, on the latent scale. |
| `standard_error` | `float` | latent units per coefficient unit | yes: not fitted | sqrt of the diagonal of H^-1, H = -d2 l / d beta2 at the estimate (l the log-likelihood with the random effects integrated out). With nothing counted, (X' V^-1 X)^-1 as stats fit-mixed reports under reml. |
| `df` | `float` | degrees of freedom | yes: not fitted, or the containment df is not positive (a group-level coefficient with too few groups) | Denominator df of the t test, by nlme's containment rule over the samples with a response of either kind, a whole number. |
| `t` | `float` | standard errors | yes: not fitted | Wald statistic, estimate / standard_error. Reported even when df is null. |
| `p_value` | `float` | fraction (0 to 1) | yes: not fitted, or df is null | Two-sided p-value of the t test on df. Not adjusted across features. |
| `residual_variance` | `float` | squared latent units | yes: not fitted | sigma^2, the run-to-run variance of the latent within a group: estimated, or the value given (residual_variance_given). The same in every coefficient block. |
| `residual_variance_given` | `bool` | — | never | True when residual_variance is the value the --residual-variance file gave, not an estimate. Reported whatever the status. |
| `group_variance` | `float` | squared latent units | yes: not fitted | tau^2, the between-group variance of the random intercept. 0 is the boundary estimate. The same in every coefficient block. |
| `log_likelihood` | `float` | log-likelihood (natural log) | yes: not fitted | The maximized log-likelihood: under reml the Laplace-approximated restricted likelihood (exactly the restricted likelihood when nothing is counted), under ml the full one. The same in every coefficient block. |
| `measured` | `int` | samples | never | Samples with a finite response for this feature. |
| `counted` | `int` | samples | never | Samples with a count for this feature. |
| `groups` | `int` | groups | never | Distinct groups among this feature's samples with a response of either kind. |

Fields of `link`:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `intercept` | `float` | natural log-odds | never | a: the per-trial log-odds at latent 0 and depth 0. |
| `slope` | `float` | natural log-odds per latent unit | never | b: how fast the per-trial log-odds follow the latent; 1 for the identity link, below 1 when the chance of a success rises more slowly than the latent. |
| `depth_slope` | `float` | natural log-odds per depth unit | never | c: the depth term's coefficient; 0 when the link has none. |
| `overdispersion` | `float` | fraction (intra-cell correlation, 0 to < 1) | never | rho, the correlation of trials within one cell (beta-binomial); 0 is the binomial. |

### Errors

| Kind | pyMzLib raises | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | neither --responses nor --counts; design, groups or link missing; a file given without a value or not found; a table empty, header-only or with too few columns; a row whose field count differs from its header; an empty or repeated feature id, sample or coefficient name; a response cell that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN); a count cell that is not two whole numbers k/n; a design cell that is not a finite number |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | the counts' features or samples are not exactly the responses' (each difference named); the design's, the groups' or the depth file's samples are not exactly the fit's; the groups or depth file with other than two columns; a depth that is not a number; a residual-variance id that is not a feature, or a value that is not a number; no coefficient on stdin, one named twice, or one not in the design; --link not identity or 2 to 4 numbers; --estimator other than reml or ml; --threads 0 or below -1 |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | mzLib refuses the input (its ArgumentException, reclassified): a cell both measured and counted, or a count with no trials or more successes than trials, named by 0-based position and then by feature and sample name; a link with a slope of 0, a non-finite value or overdispersion outside [0, 1); a link with a depth term and no --depth; a depth that is not finite; a given residual variance that is not positive and finite; a design not of full column rank; an empty group label |
| `correctness` | [`BridgeError`][pymzlib.BridgeError] | never expected |
| `service_unavailable` | [`ServiceUnavailableError`][pymzlib.ServiceUnavailableError] | never raised by this verb |

### Caveats

- A random intercept per group on a latent scale: a measured sample reads the latent; a counted sample has k of n trials succeed with logit g = intercept + slope x latent + depth_slope x depth, binomially or beta-binomially. No random slopes, nested or crossed groupings.
- Responses and estimates are on the latent scale (natural log-odds for a logit latent), not fractions or intensities. Which cells are counted, and the link, are the caller's modelling choices; the bridge builds neither (stats fit-link fits a link).
- Counted samples are integrated by adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature (40 nodes over the group intercept, 12 over each count's residual), measured ones exactly. mzLib agrees with lme4's glmer (nAGQ 25, ML) to about 1e-6, with lmer to about 1e-5 when nothing is counted, and with glmmTMB to its Laplace error (about 1% in tau^2 and standard errors, 5% in sigma^2) when sigma^2 is estimated from counts alone (ReferenceComparisonLogitNormalTests).
- Fixed effects are tested by Wald t on nlme's containment df, over samples with a response of either kind. standard_error is at the estimated variances and does not include their uncertainty, so it is not glmmTMB's vcov().
- Under reml the fixed effects are integrated out by a Laplace approximation (glmmTMB's REML = TRUE); it is exact when nothing is counted. Under REML glmmTMB reports beta as the joint mode of (beta, u), so compare its estimates with this verb's ml ones only.
- With nothing counted the model is stats fit-mixed's, fitted by a different optimiser: under reml the numbers agree with fit-mixed's to about 1e-5; under ml estimates and variances agree, but standard errors are at the ML variances, where fit-mixed's scale by RSS / (observed - coefficients) as nlme's summary does.
- separated is a status, never a p-value: the counts are (quasi-)completely separated by the design and the estimate runs to infinity.
- p_value is not adjusted across features. Send one coefficient's p_value column to stats adjust for Benjamini-Hochberg.

### Example

```python
fit = pymzlib.stats.fit_latent_mixed('lnmm_reference_design.tsv', 'lnmm_reference_groups.tsv', ['Intercept', 'trait', 'x'], link='identity', counts='lnmm_scatter_counts.tsv')
```

```python
fit = pymzlib.stats.fit_latent_mixed('lnmm_reference_design.tsv', 'lnmm_reference_groups.tsv', ['Intercept', 'trait', 'x'], link=(-0.4, 0.6, 0.3), counts='lnmm_link_counts.tsv', depth='lnmm_link_depth.tsv', residual_variance='lnmm_link_residual_variance.tsv', estimator='ml')
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`stats_fit_latent_mixed_link_ml.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/stats_fit_latent_mixed_link_ml.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.

```python
fit = pymzlib.stats.fit_latent_mixed('lnmm_simulated_design.tsv', 'lnmm_simulated_groups.tsv', ['Intercept', 'trait'], link=(0.4, 0.6), responses='lnmm_simulated_responses.tsv', counts='lnmm_simulated_counts.tsv')
```

### References

- [doi:10.1080/01621459.1993.10594284](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1993.10594284): generalized linear mixed models, the class of model this verb fits: a latent linear predictor with a random intercept, observed through a binomial link (Breslow and Clayton, J Am Stat Assoc 88:9, 1993)
- [doi:10.1093/biomet/81.3.624](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/81.3.624): adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature, centred at the integrand's mode and scaled by its curvature, which mzLib uses to integrate the counted samples (Liu and Pierce, Biometrika 81:624, 1994)
- [doi:10.18637/jss.v067.i01](https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v067.i01): lme4's lmer and glmer (nAGQ 25), the references mzLib's fits are held to (Bates, Maechler, Bolker and Walker, J Stat Softw 67:1, 2015)
- [doi:10.32614/RJ-2017-066](https://doi.org/10.32614/RJ-2017-066): glmmTMB, whose Laplace-approximated REML mzLib's REML follows and whose fits with run scatter are a reference (Brooks et al., R Journal 9:378, 2017)
- [doi:10.1093/biomet/58.3.545](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/58.3.545): restricted maximum likelihood, the default estimator (Patterson and Thompson, Biometrika 58:545, 1971)
- [doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1948.tb00014.x](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1948.tb00014.x): the beta-binomial distribution, which a link with overdispersion gives a count cell (Skellam, J R Stat Soc B 10:257, 1948)
